\begin{abstract}
Noisy supervision makes a fine-tuned model memorize wrong labels. We filter samples by the angle between the
per-sample gradient $\partial \ell_i / \partial \theta$ and a reference gradient. At a noise rate of 0.2 the
accuracy rises by 2.1 points on three benchmarks (Table 2).
\end{abstract}

\section{Method}
The filter keeps sample $i$ when its cosine with the reference gradient is at least $\tau$. The reference
gradient comes from 64 verified samples. It is recomputed every 50 steps, which costs one extra backward pass.

\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} noisy supervision, gradient alignment

\section{Conclusion}
The rule raises accuracy by 2.1 points at a noise rate of 0.2 (Table 2).
\end{document}
